mechanisms.explanation: The starting design's smallest valve size (23 mm nominal) only covers an annulus range down to a minimum of 21 mm. Across the development set, 26 hearts fail with no-fit under the annulus-coverage rule because their annulus is below 21 mm (6 hearts in the 18-20 mm band and 20 no-fit hearts in the 20-22 mm band). Profiling these 26 hearts shows globally smaller aortic root and outflow dimensions compared to the rest of the cohort: mean annulusMm is 20.3111913883671 vs 24.9324454320138 (effect size -1.86851326058083), mean lvotMm is 18.6541907417738 vs 24.5914581882067 (effect size -1.76612687101239), mean sinusMm is 28.3291265352961 vs 33.1405932624916 (effect size -1.44492671211772), mean aorticValveArea is 38.2573117767538 vs 65.9337976553416 (effect size -1.27049733981414), mean lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio is 0.845935537553593 vs 0.970976897026051 (effect size -1.16659320840679), mean sinotubularJunctionMm is 26.4691521877821 vs 29.7823829953359 (effect size -1.14416262377827), and mean sinusHeightMm is 22.1538461538462 vs 25.3823529411765 (effect size -0.968535359374452). For example, heart-013 has an annulusMm of 20.3602109283815, failing the 21 mm limit by a margin of -0.639789071618548.

mechanisms.title: Disproportionately Narrow Sinotubular Junction Relative to Annulus Size (stj-excess)
mechanisms.explanation: Across all three assigned valve sizes (23 mm, 25 mm, and 27 mm), 52 hearts are placed at risk by the stj-excess rule because their sinotubular junction (STJ) diameter is too narrow for the assigned nominal valve size. Inspection of individual hearts shows the required minimum STJ limits are 25 mm for the 23 mm valve (heart-018 measured 23.9075688982299, margin -1.09243110177013), 27 mm for the 25 mm valve (heart-086 measured 26.48261056391, margin -0.517389436090028), and 29 mm for the 27 mm valve (heart-014 measured 26.8311463740637, margin -2.16885362593629). Profiling these 52 hearts shows that while their annulusMm is comparable to the rest of the cohort (mean 24.2162817933461 vs 24.6941922828066, effect size -0.193233715024884), they have disproportionately narrow upper roots with a markedly smaller sinotubularJunctionMm (mean 26.5045097370466 vs 30.0246399161251, difference -3.52013017907853, effect size -1.2156114728117), smaller sinusMm (mean 30.5892482692222 vs 33.1623513220977, effect size -0.772725978362664), and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (mean 1.02645440665182 vs 0.953344983673109, effect size 0.682085964814614).

mechanisms.title: Shallow and Short Sinus of Valsalva Geometry Relative to Annulus Size (sinus-clearance)
mechanisms.explanation: Across all three valve sizes, 38 hearts are placed at risk by the sinus-clearance rule because their sinus of Valsalva diameter (sinusMm) is insufficient for the assigned nominal valve size. Profiling these 38 hearts demonstrates a constricted, short aortic root geometry relative to their annulus: compared to the rest of the cohort, they have a substantially smaller sinusMm (mean 29.0481355368023 vs 33.2246133140638, difference -4.17647777726146, effect size -1.25423382205296), smaller sinotubularJunctionMm (mean 26.7830986506325 vs 29.8592581447899, effect size -1.06229445590425), shorter sinusHeightMm (mean 22.0921052631579 vs 25.4958563535912, difference -3.40375109043327, effect size -1.02110774508236), and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (mean 1.02620177062988 vs 0.956198939724312, effect size 0.653102521023595), while annulusMm is only slightly smaller (mean 23.6526731338521 vs 24.7348728966418, effect size -0.437566207845688).

Individual heart inspections show the required minimum sinusMm limits are 28 mm for the 23 mm valve (heart-018 measured 26.3006749541182, margin -1.69932504588178), 30 mm for the 25 mm valve (heart-086 measured 28.6100927234801, margin -1.38990727651987), and 32 mm for the 27 mm valve (heart-014 measured 30.7778575461286, margin -1.22214245387135). Profiling these 38 hearts demonstrates a constricted, short aortic root geometry relative to their annulus: compared to the rest of the cohort, they have a substantially smaller sinusMm (mean 29.0481355368023 vs 33.2246133140638, difference -4.17647777726146, effect size -1.25423382205296), smaller sinotubularJunctionMm (mean 26.7830986506325 vs 29.8592581447899, effect size -1.06229445590425), shorter sinusHeightMm (mean 22.0921052631579 vs 25.4958563535912, difference -3.40375109043327, effect size -1.02110774508236), and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (mean 1.02620177062988 vs 0.956198939724312, effect size 0.653102521023595), while annulusMm is only slightly smaller (mean 23.6526731338521 vs 24.7348728966418, effect size -0.437566207845688).

findings.title: Small Aortic Root Anatomy Below Minimum Annulus Coverage (< 21 mm)
findings.explanation: The starting design's smallest valve size (23 mm nominal) only covers an annulus range down to a minimum of 21 mm. Across the development set, 26 hearts fail with no-fit under the annulus-coverage rule because their annulus is below 21 mm (6 hearts in the 18-20 mm band and 20 no-fit hearts in the 20-22 mm band). Profiling these 26 hearts shows globally smaller aortic root and outflow dimensions compared to the rest of the cohort: mean annulusMm is 20.3111913883671 vs 24.9324454320138 (effect size -1.86851326058083), mean lvotMm is 18.6541907417738 vs 24.5914581882067 (effect size -1.76612687101239), mean sinusMm is 28.3291265352961 vs 33.1405932624916 (effect size -1.44492671211772), mean aorticValveArea is 38.2573117767538 vs 65.9337976553416 (effect size -1.27049733981414), mean lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio is 0.845935537553593 vs 0.970976897026051 (effect size -1.16659320840679), mean sinotubularJunctionMm is 26.4691521877821 vs 29.7823829953359 (effect size -1.14416262377827), and mean sinusHeightMm is 22.1538461538462 vs 25.3823529411765 (effect size -0.968535359374452). For example, heart-013 has an annulusMm of 20.3602109283815, failing the 21 mm limit by a margin of -0.639789071618548.

findings.title: Large Aortic Root Anatomy Exceeding Maximum Annulus Coverage (> 27 mm)
findings.explanation: The starting design's largest valve size (27 mm nominal) only covers an annulus range up to a maximum of 27 mm. Across the development set, 67 hearts fail with no-fit under the annulus-coverage rule because their annulus exceeds 27 mm (30 no-fit hearts in the 26-28 mm band, 31 in the 28-30 mm band, and 6 in the 30-32 mm band). Profiling these 67 hearts reveals globally enlarged root and outflow tract anatomy compared to the rest of the cohort: mean annulusMm is 28.3736793853115 vs 23.8792463929575 (effect size 1.81723566064299), mean lvotMm is 29.1834336521146 vs 23.203976777729 (effect size 1.7786767322157), mean sinusMm is 36.9204307212132 vs 32.0044153506555 (effect size 1.47632360958678), mean sinotubularJunctionMm is 32.6361463160546 vs 28.9495116935805 (effect size 1.27311068487743), mean lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio is 1.05926460340551 vs 0.943450315423325 (effect size 1.08050778051756), mean aorticValveArea is 81.5480622670355 vs 60.6312620342401 (effect size 0.960191953912409), and mean sinusHeightMm is 27.5373134328358 vs 24.6966966966967 (effect size 0.852170347659889). For example, heart-019 has an annulusMm of 27.3588421207855, failing the 27 mm maximum limit by a margin of -0.358842120785503.

findings.title: Disproportionately Narrow Sinotubular Junction Relative to Annulus Size (stj-excess)
findings.explanation: Across all three assigned valve sizes (23 mm, 25 mm, and 27 mm), 52 hearts are placed at risk by the stj-excess rule because their sinotubular junction (STJ) diameter is too narrow for the assigned nominal valve size. Inspection of individual hearts shows the required minimum STJ limits are 25 mm for the 23 mm valve (heart-018 measured 23.9075688982299, margin -1.09243110177013), 27 mm for the 25 mm valve (heart-086 measured 26.48261056391, margin -0.517389436090028), and 29 mm for the 27 mm valve (heart-014 measured 26.8311463740637, margin -2.16885362593629). Profiling these 52 hearts shows that while their annulusMm is comparable to the rest of the cohort (mean 24.2162817933461 vs 24.6941922828066, effect size -0.193233715024884), they have disproportionately narrow upper roots with a markedly smaller sinotubularJunctionMm (mean 26.5045097370466 vs 30.0246399161251, difference -3.52013017907853, effect size -1.2156114728117), smaller sinusMm (mean 30.5892482692222 vs 33.1623513220977, effect size -0.772725978362664), and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (mean 1.02645440665182 vs 0.953344983673109, effect size 0.682085964814614).
